pattern.crimePattern: a fish buyer who lends against catches kills the co-op chairman who signed with a rival buyer, then stages a drowning in the night storm
pattern.notes: Fictional co-op, buyers and company ("Sibiloi Fresh"). Lake Turkana's night winds and alkaline water are described for the cultural reader to check.

ob.text: The fishermen's co-operative at Loiyangalani reports its chairman, Ekal Lokwawi (41), drowned in Sunday night's storm. His boat was found capsized in the shallows at dawn, the body beside it.

people.name: Ekal Lokwawi
people.bio: Wrote the landing-register rule himself: no boat goes out at night unsigned.

facts.text: Ekal Lokwawi was found dead in the shallows at dawn beside his capsized boat, "drowned in the storm".
He lay face down in 30 cm of water beside his boat, with one blow to the back of the head.
His nets are folded and dry under the thwart: no weed, no scales, no fish.
Both oars are in the boat, unmarked; the gunwale's edge is clean.
There is no white alkaline crust on his skin or collar above the waterline; his clothes are wet only where they lay in the water.
Sand drifted against every boat and post on the beach overnight, but none against the body or the boat's windward side.
Ewoi: one person in tyre-sole sandals walked backwards from the fish store to the water, dragging something heavy on a mat, after the wind dropped (about 04:30–05:30).
Co-op fish store: the floor has been swept, but there is a dark stain soaked into the earth under a fresh layer of sand.
One wooden fish club is missing from the rack of twelve by the store door.
Landing register, Sunday: six boats signed out 18:00–19:30. Ekal's boat, "Napak", is not signed out. Akuwom closed the book at 19:30.
On Friday Ekal signed the co-op's fresh fish to Sibiloi Fresh of Kitale, and posted a notice: "Loice's advances can be repaid in cash."
The co-op cash box is locked and matches the book.
Akuwom: every boat that fishes at night signs out; Ekal wrote the rule. A boat that fished a windy night comes back with wet, tangled nets and scales in the bilge.
Akuwom: the lake is bitter water. Anyone soaked in it and left to dry has a fine white crust on skin and clothes.
Akuwom: the easterly blew from six until near dawn. It piles sand against everything on the beach.
Akuwom: Ekal and his brother Lokol quarrelled over who owned the boat, their father's.
Akuwom: last month Ekal accused the treasurer, Joyce, of a cash shortfall. She found the money.
Akuwom closed the register at 19:30 and was home with his family all night.
Records, Loice's line: the mast covers the whole shore; at 04:12 on Monday she called her truck driver. The driver: "She said, don't come before seven."
Behind Loice's sacks: tyre-sole sandals with beach sand still in the treads.
A palm-fibre drying mat, damp and stained.
The missing fish club from the co-op rack, washed.
Loice's ledger: KSh 1.4 million lent to 38 fishermen against their catches.
Mama Lokiru: Lomulen drank in her bar from 19:00 until she closed at 01:00, then slept on the bench.
Lokol's wife and neighbours: he was at a goat slaughter for a wedding until late, then home.
The mission sisters: Joyce taught the adult literacy class until 21:00, then stayed the night with them while the sand blew.
Post-mortem: one blow to the back of the head with a heavy wooden object, fatal.
Post-mortem: no water in the lungs, no froth in the airways. He was dead before he entered the water.
Post-mortem: death on Sunday between 20:00 and 22:00.
Lab: Ekal's blood in the store-floor stain and on the mat.
Lab: the drag-mark prints match Loice's sandals, including a cut in the left heel.
Missing: his nets are dry, and the register has no entry for his boat.
Missing: there is no alkaline crust on his clothes.
Missing: there is no drifted sand against the body or the boat.
Missing: there are no fish or scales in the boat.
Missing: there is no lake water in his lungs.

interrogations.intro: Loice sits on a sack of dried tilapia with her ledger closed on her knee. "I was at home all night. I didn't see Ekal after Friday. And Sibiloi Fresh doesn't worry me. My fishermen are loyal."
Lomulen sits on the bar bench, not looking up. "We went out together at eight. The wind turned the boat over and he went in. I swam to shore."
Lokol stands at the water's edge with his blanket pulled round him. "The boat was our father's. We fought about it. I was at a wedding."
Joyce holds the cash book to her chest. "He accused me of a shortfall. I found the money. I was at the mission."

contradictions.reaction: "I was drunk. I never went to the beach. When they found him I was afraid they'd say I left him alone. I said the first thing."
Loice opens the ledger and closes it again. "I went to talk business. He laughed at me in front of my own debts. That's all I'll say."
She looks at the notice on the photograph: advances repaid in cash. "Thirty-eight of them owe me," she says. "Thirty-eight."

reconstruction.text: For years Loice has bought nearly all the co-op's dried fish and lent the fishermen cash against their catches. On Friday Ekal signs the co-op to Sibiloi Fresh and tells the fishermen they can repay her in cash.
Sunday, about 20:30, in the wind. Loice meets Ekal at the co-op fish store to argue. He laughs. She takes a club from the rack by the door.
She sweeps sand over the stain and waits. At 04:12 she tells her driver not to come before seven.
About 04:30, when the wind drops, she drags him on a palm-fibre mat 80 metres to the shallows, rolls him in beside his boat, and tips the boat over.
Lomulen, drunk on the bar bench all night, wakes to the news and tells the co-op they went out together.

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: records on Loice and a warrant on her store. Detain her after the search; blood (12 h) and tread (8 h) each take 4 h more to reach the lab, still inside 24 h. The post-mortem drive to Marsabit runs in parallel.
